sentences.text: Ammonitritor is an extinct early ichthyosauriform that belongs to the family Omphalosauridae and lived in the Early Triassic Olenekian Vikinghøgda Formation of Norway.
The only known specimen preserves a nearly complete skull together with a partial vertebral column.
It is the first omphalosaurid discovered with a three-dimensional skull, whereas other members have flattened skulls.
The fossil material was uncovered by Felix Saludes during a 2010 expedition led by Luc Ebbo on the northwest slope of Vikinghøgda mountain, Svalbard, Norway.
The specimen, catalogued as PGE LE 2024.0.264, is curated in Luc Ebbo's Paléogalerie in Salignac, France.
Although the skull is partially disarticulated and missing the braincase and palate, the preserved elements retain their original three-dimensional shape.
Like other omphalosaurids, Ammonitritor possessed dense maxillary and dentary tooth batteries that were suited for grinding hard-shelled cephalopods such as ammonoids.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ammonitritor within Omphalosauridae, diverging after Cartorhynchus and before Sclerocormus and Omphalosaurus.
